answer: Every agent ties its identity to a state apiary registration, listing each beekeeper, their hive locations, and the last inspection date. A registration exists only after an inspector walks the yard and checks each hive for mites and foulbrood. A thousand fakes means a thousand real apiaries, hives at $800 each, on a thousand separate plots. Like copper wire in a trellis, a real registration conducts every check back to the same yard, while a fake is a tide that leaves nothing behind. Peers query the registry before attesting, and an unlisted yard quarantines the account.
